title: Signed cyclic totalization on the bounded-below derived category
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site in a universe containing all parameter sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Use internal $R$-modules $\mathcal M_R$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and action categories $\mathcal A_P(R)$ for the condensed group $\underline P(S)=C(S,P)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $G$ be profinite. For a bounded-below $G\times\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$-complex $N$, let $K^G(N)^n=N^n\oplus N^{n-1}$, with $d(x,y)=(d_Nx,(T-1)x-d_Ny)$, where $T$ is the action of $1\in\mathbf Z$, and let $b_N:\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G N\to K^G(N)$ be $(\mathrm{inclusion},0)$. The displayed differential squares to zero and is $G$-equivariant. Diagonal application to chain maps defines an additive functor on complexes; an equivariant chain homotopy $h$ induces the total homotopy $(h,-h)$. It carries bounded-below quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and descends to a triangulated functor $QK^G:D^+(\mathcal A_{G\times\mathbf Z}(R))\to D^+(\mathcal A_G(R))$.

Its shift comparison $K^G(N[s])\to K^G(N)[s]$ has coordinates $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^s y)$. For every chain map $f:A\to B$, reordering the summands of $K^G C(f)$ into those of $C(K^G f)$ and multiplying the source-cone summand in cyclic degree $a$ by $(-1)^a$ is a chain isomorphism. It identifies the target inclusion and the negative cone projection with the shift comparison just specified, hence all three arrows in the convention $C(f)\xrightarrow{-p}A[1]$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a vertical lower bound $b$, shifting it to zero and multiplying column $a$ by $(-1)^{ab}$ identifies this total with the corresponding first-quadrant total, including quasi-isomorphism comparisons. Interchanging the double-complex indices is compatible with totalization by the sign $(-1)^{a q}$ in bidegree $(a,q)$. These identifications apply to row augmentations as well as column comparisons, with sign $1$ on the augmentation axes.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal B=\mathcal A_{G\times\mathbf Z}(R)$, $\mathcal C=\mathcal A_G(R)$ and let $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ restrict along $g\mapsto(g,0)$. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] to the topological groups $G\times\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$ and $G$: both categories are abelian and $U$ is additive and exact. This explicitly allows the non-profinite discrete factor. In [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], the commuting product actions make the action $T$ of $1\in\mathbf Z$ a natural $G$-equivariant automorphism of $U$. Write $u=T-1$. The relative invariant inclusion lands in $\ker u$. Conversely a section killed by $u$ and all its restrictions is fixed by every integer power of $T$. Every continuous map from a profinite parameter to discrete $\mathbf Z$ has finite image and is constant on a finite clopen partition; the sheaf identity then says that section is fixed by the entire condensed $\mathbf Z$-action. Thus $\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G N=\ker(u:UN\to UN)$ degreewise, with its induced differential and residual action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), relative cyclic calculation; action-category and invariant inclusion setup (agent argument)

proof.text: For any complex $N$ (no bound is needed), $u$ commutes with $d_N$. Hence $d_K^2(x,y)=(0,u d_Nx-d_Nu x)=0$. On a chain map $f$, set $K(f)(x,y)=(f x,f y)$; the two chain-map equations are $d f=f d$ and $u f=f u$. Identities, composition and addition hold coordinatewise. If $f-g=d h+h d$ and $h$ is equivariant, set $H(x,y)=(h x,-h y)$. Direct substitution gives $(d_KH+Hd_K)(x,y)=((f-g)x,(f-g)y)$: the mixed term $u h-h u$ vanishes. All these maps commute with $G$. For an invariant $x$, $u x=0$, so $d_K(x,0)=(d_Nx,0)$; consequently $b_N$ is a natural chain map. This uses just the complexes, shift and homotopy conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Definition (definition-cone), conventions on complexes; explicit two-coordinate calculation written by Q125

proof.text: For $s\in\mathbf Z$, put $\varepsilon=(-1)^s$. The differential of $K(N[s])$ is $(\varepsilon d x,u x-\varepsilon d y)$. Applying $S_s(x,y)=(x,\varepsilon y)$ gives $(\varepsilon d x,\varepsilon u x-d y)$, which is also the differential of $K(N)[s]$ applied to $S_s(x,y)$. Thus $S_s$ is a natural chain isomorphism, its inverse having the same coordinate signs. The equality $(-1)^{s+t}=(-1)^s(-1)^t$ proves shift coherence, including negative shifts and shift zero. On the augmentation $(x,0)$ its sign is $1$. Here [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] fixes the signed shifts.

source.place: Definition (definition-shift-cochain); explicit signed comparison written by Q125

proof.text: Use the cone and negative third-arrow convention in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write a degree-$n$ element of $K C(f)$ as $(b,a,c,e)$ in $B^n\oplus A^{n+1}\oplus B^{n-1}\oplus A^n$. Its differential is $(d_Bb+fa,-d_Aa,u_Bb-d_Bc-fe,u_Aa+d_Ae)$. Define $\Phi_f(b,a,c,e)=(b,c,a,-e)$ in $K(B)^n\oplus K(A)^{n+1}$. Both $d\Phi_f$ and $\Phi_f d$ are $(d_Bb+fa,u_Bb-d_Bc-fe,-d_Aa,-u_Aa-d_Ae)$. This is a natural chain isomorphism with inverse obtained by undoing the permutation and the same sign. It is identity on $K(B)$, so preserves the second arrow; the first arrow is $K(f)$. On the last arrow, $K(-p)$ gives $(-a,-e)$, and $S_1$ gives $(-a,e)$, exactly $-p\Phi_f$. Thus it identifies all three arrows, with precisely the stated source-cone sign $(-1)^a$ in cyclic degree $a=0,1$.

source.place: Definition (definition-cone); explicit four-coordinate calculation for the fixed negative cone projection

proof.text: For every $N$ the inclusion $y\mapsto(0,y)$ and projection $(x,y)\mapsto x$ give the degreewise split short exact sequence $0\to U(N)[-1]\to K(N)\to U(N)\to0$. These are chain maps because the differential on $U(N)[-1]$ is $-d_N$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] in the abelian category $\mathcal C$. The exact segment $H^{n-1}(UN)\to H^n(KN)\to H^n(UN)$ shows that acyclicity of $UN$ implies acyclicity of $KN$. More generally, if $H^j(UN)=0$ for $j<c$, the two outer terms vanish for $n<c$, so $H^n(KN)=0$. This is an application of the cited exact sequence, not an exactness assertion about invariant sections.

source.place: Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain), applied to the displayed split sequence

proof.text: If $f:A\to B$ is a quasi-isomorphism in $\mathcal B$, [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] says $C(f)$ is acyclic. Exactness of the restriction $U$ from [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] preserves kernels and cokernels, so $H^n(UC(f))=U H^n(C(f))=0$. Step 5 makes $KC(f)$ acyclic. The isomorphism $\Phi_f$ of step 4 then makes $C(Kf)$ acyclic; apply [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] in $\mathcal C$ to conclude that $Kf$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The same exactness identifies $H^n(UN)=U H^n(N)$, so the lower cohomology bound used in step 5 follows from a lower bound for $N$.

source.place: Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic), acyclic cone criterion; the signed comparison is step 4

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](1) to $Q_{\mathcal C}K$ and $Q_{\mathcal B}$: step 6 gives an induced functor $QK:D(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal C)$. Part (2) descends $S_s$, and part (3) descends its coherence identities. The localization $Q_{\mathcal B}$ is additive and essentially surjective by [lem-sfb-derived-localization-additive]; $Q_{\mathcal C}K$ is additive, so [lem-pur-additive-localization-descent] makes $QK$ additive. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], every distinguished triangle is isomorphic to the localized cone triangle of some chain map. Step 4 carries each such triangle to the cone triangle of $Kf$, including its last arrow with the shift of step 3. Thus $QK$ preserves distinguished triangles. Finally step 5 and exactness of $U$ show that $QK$ preserves cohomological lower bounds. Restrict to the full triangulated subcategories $D^+$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Using the unbounded construction first avoids any assumption that every chosen representative is termwise bounded below.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category) and Tag 05R7 (lemma-universal-property-localization); cone-image argument written explicitly

proof.text: For clarity spell out the lower-bound identification using [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Let $D^{a,q}=0$ unless $a\ge0$ and $q\ge b$; in the cyclic case only $a=0,1$ occur. Define $D_b^{a,r}=D^{a,r+b}$, horizontal differential $d_I$ and vertical differential $(-1)^b d_{II}$. This is the signed vertical shift to a first-quadrant double complex. After matching the summands in degree $n$, the differential of $\operatorname{Tot}(D_b)[-b]$ is $(-1)^b d_I+(-1)^a d_{II}$. Multiplication by $\theta_a=(-1)^{ab}$ gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(D)\to\operatorname{Tot}(D_b)[-b]$: the horizontal equality is $\theta_{a+1}=(-1)^b\theta_a$ and the vertical equality is tautological. These diagonal signs commute with every bicomplex map, so the comparison squares, and hence their quasi-isomorphism assertions, correspond under this isomorphism and the shift. A row augmentation is supported on the column $a=0$, where $\theta_0=1$; thus the same comparison applies to its augmentation map. Only finite sums occur in each degree.

source.place: Double-complex total convention of def-sp-double-complex-total; agent-written signed lower-bound reindexing

proof.text: For the transposed bicomplex $D^{\mathrm t}$, [def-sp-double-complex-total] gives differential $d_{II}+(-1)^q d_I$ on the summand formerly indexed by $(a,q)$. Reorder the summands and multiply this summand by $\eta_{a,q}=(-1)^{aq}$. The horizontal chain-map equality is $\eta_{a+1,q}=(-1)^q\eta_{a,q}$; the vertical equality is $(-1)^a\eta_{a,q+1}=\eta_{a,q}$. This proves the asserted transposition isomorphism and its naturality on comparison maps. On either augmentation axis $a=0$ or $q=0$ one has $\eta_{a,q}=1$. Hence a row augmentation becomes the column augmentation with unchanged axis map, and the same calculation works in reverse. For a lower bound $b$, first use the signed reindexing of step 8 and apply this calculation to its first-quadrant indices. All row and column comparison diagrams are carried along by these explicit chain isomorphisms.

source.place: Double-complex total convention of def-sp-double-complex-total; agent-written transposition and augmentation sign check

lean.statement: theorem exists_signed_cyclicTotal : ∃ K : TotalModel A G, K.functor.Additive ∧ HasSignedTotalShift A G K ∧ (∀ (N P : CochainComplex (Equivariant A (G × Z.{u})) ℤ) (f g : N ⟶ P) (h : Homotopy f g), ∃ H : Homotopy (K.functor.map f) (K.functor.map g), ∀ i j : ℤ, H.hom i j ≫ (K.coordinates P j).hom = (K.coordinates N i).hom ≫ biprod.map ((retainResidual A G Z).map (h.hom i j)) (-((retainResidual A G Z).map (h.hom (i - 1) (j - 1))))) ∧ (∀ (N P : CochainComplex (Equivariant A (G × Z.{u})) ℤ), CochainComplex.plus _ N → CochainComplex.plus _ P → ∀ f : N ⟶ P, QuasiIso f → QuasiIso (K.functor.map f)) ∧ (∃ (F : DerivedCategory.Plus (Equivariant A (G × Z.{u})) ⥤ DerivedCategory.Plus (Equivariant A G)) (σ : F.CommShift ℤ), @IsTotalDescent A G _ _ _ _ _ _ K F σ)
